newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower but losses pared.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower but losses pared.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures ended mostly lower but late short covering by a local with cash connections in the hog pit and scattered local short covering in pork bellies pared losses near the close, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.525 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher with June off most at 83.900 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.400 cent lower to 0.450 higher with only March up and July off 1.125 at 90.725 cents.
A local in the hog pit kept hog futures from easing on steady to weak cash hog expectations for Tuesday and on overbought conditions in hogs linked to the Taiwan pork ban, traders said.

Just as producers are holding back more hogs for breeding than in months past, and shipping fewer animals due to their preoccupation with spring planting, packers are cutting slaughter rates. Packer margins remain poor due to slow domestic demand for pork which followed a jump in prices after the Taiwan pork ban was announced.
The local buying offset early selling by Cargill Investor Services, Dean Witter, LIT division of First Options, Rand Financials and Lind-Waldock in June, traders said.
Cargill, Rand and Rosenthal sold July early and Lind-Waldock sold August, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought August 74 puts and Dean Witter sold the June 85 straddle early, pit sources added.

Pork bellies were pulled off the lows by late local short covering. But prices remained sharply lower on floor talk that cash bellies were trading as much as $5 per cwt lower. The USDA reported cash bellies as untraded and left cash at a nominal $90 early Monday, but talk persisted that sales were occuring at $85, they said.
The recent runup in cash bellies to highest prices since mid-August apparently cut off domestic demand, they said.
Cash bellies moved up to $90 per cwt for 14-16 lb bellies late last week, the highest price level since August 14.

Continued relatively light hog slaughter and rolling of long positions into July from May as well as some rolling of longs into August from July, reinforced summer months before the local buying pared losses, they added.

Refco and Cargill Investor Services sold May early. LFG notably bought July at the start before local and commission house selling pressured that month, traders said. Spike Trading sold July late while buying August, pit sources said.
